summary:
The core holds up against the tree. ScanStore.Unfinished, AtLeast and AtLeastFigures are as the design says. The tracker seeds row i as entry _first+i. TopLevelSnapshot.cs may not name ScanStore, and only TopLevelTracker.cs may set Revised. The timer stops before line 301, and ShowStoppedList redraws from _shownTopLevel, so the marked snapshot survives switching views. The new TopLevelRow members pass the snapshot-immutability patterns. Three things will cost rework.
(1) The tree header now promises 'a figure with no mark is final', but every tree row still draws an unmarked share percentage (ShareText). Those percentages are not final whenever the row or its parent is unfinished, which is almost every row after a Stop.
(2) Both headers are one line trimmed with an ellipsis. T-010 measured 109 of 201 characters drawn at 880 px and 48 at 560 px. The new at-least clause sits after about 110 characters of lead in the list header and after 43 in the tree header, so the explanation is cut off at the default size. T-013 checks only that the header string contains the clause, which passes even though the clause is never drawn.
(3) The measured trap of putting 'at least' on a rolled figure is guarded by a regex with holes (this.OnDisk, a local variable, r.Bytes). It could instead be made impossible to write, by giving AtLeastSize a parameter of the store's bound type. The design calls the duplicate TopLevelAtLeast contract expensive to reverse.
Smaller points:
- The validate list leaves out the rules harness (Q-027), T-003 (Q-128) and the rest of the existing window cases that criterion 6 names.
- The fail-loud throw at line 301 is outside Q-071's per-pass containment.
- The argument for criterion 6 ignores Unfinished's NotListedAtOrBelow arm. On a real completed store that arm is the risk spike's own question, and that spike did not finish.
- No mutant shows that the 'drawn equals bound, not rolled' check or the cell-fit check can fail.
I checked the one load-bearing recalled outside claim, that OneTime bindings are re-evaluated when the DataContext changes, and the source supports it. The Elasticsearch prior art is decoration and I left it alone.

findings.claim: The design leaves Share, ShareText and the bars unchanged. It then writes into the tree header 'Figures marked at least are all that is certain; a figure with no mark is final', and the slice goal is 'any figure without a mark is final'. But every non-root tree row with figures draws ShareText, a percentage such as '45.0 %' from ShareText.Percent. That number is the row's listed (rolled) on-disk figure divided by its parent's listed figure. It is final only when both the row and its parent are final. After a Stop in the listing the root is unfinished, so every depth-1 share is non-final, and so is the share of any final child under an unfinished parent. The rolled figures it divides can also sit above the final ones (SL-112: 64 MiB against 1 MiB). So nearly every share percentage in the stopped tree is an unmarked, non-final figure sitting under a header that says unmarked figures are final. Q-290 approved rewording the headers precisely to stop that kind of false sentence. T-013's C3 checks only the Size and On disk cells, so it cannot see the problem.
findings.evidence: src/FsAnalyser.App/FolderTreeNode.cs:130 (ShareText reads Share = ChildRow.Share, rolled over rolled); src/FsAnalyser.App/FolderTreeRowText.cs:20 (Share => ShareText.Percent); design component 'Tree row at-least figures' ('Unchanged: OnDisk (the ranking value), Share, BarWidth, ShareShown') and 'Ending wiring and stopped headers' (tree header clause)
findings.fix: Narrow the tree header's promise to what is marked, for example 'Sizes marked at least are all that is certain; a size with no mark is final. Shares, bars and order are by space on disk as listed.' Alternatively, blank ShareText (keeping the bar) on rows whose parent entry is Unfinished, and add that to T-013's C3. Either way, no header sentence may cover the share column unless the share column honours it.

findings.claim: The explanation of the marks will not be drawn at the default window size. TopLevelHeader is a single line with CharacterEllipsis. SL-110 measured the stopped tree header at 109 of 201 characters drawn at 880 px, and 48 at the 560 px minimum. In the design's tree header the at-least clause starts after the 43-character lead and is about 81 characters long, so the drawn text ends near 'a figure with no m…'. Both 'mark is final' and 'by space on disk as listed' are cut. In the list headers the kept lead plus the not-read explanation already run to about 113 characters, so none of the reworded size clause is drawn at 880 px; it is reachable only through the header's tooltip. For the cells, the design measured clipping carefully (102 DIP). For the header it did not. T-013 checks that the tree header 'starts with $StoppedTreeLead and contains the at-least clause', and L-001 and L-004 compare the string with CheckEqual. All of these pass on text the person never sees. That is weaker than T-010:6637, which checks headerCharsShown for the lead. The derived SC-404 criterion, that the tree header says sizes may be off after a Stop in the size checks, is then met only in the string.
findings.evidence: src/FsAnalyser.App/MainWindow.xaml:411-412 (TextTrimming=CharacterEllipsis, tooltip = full text); .taad/slices/SL-110/build-slice-1.json:214 ('T-010 logs headerCharsShown/headerWidth at 880 px (109 of 201 characters) and at the 560 px minimum (48)'); tests/window/WindowCases.ps1:6637 (the existing drawn-characters check for the lead); tests/window/FsaWindowHook/StoppedTree.cs:333-336 (headerCharsShown already logged)
findings.fix: Tree header: keep a short at-least clause within the first ~100 characters, for example 'Not read yet: folders the stop came before. At least: not every size was read; unmarked sizes are final.' Make T-013 check headerCharsShown at 880 px is at least the clause's end index, as T-010 does for the lead. List headers: Q-290 keeps the lead, so state in the design that the size clause is reachable only through the tooltip at the default width, and do not cite L-001 or L-004 as proof that the header shows it.

findings.class_of: rolled or listing figure spellings reaching AtLeastSize
findings.claim:
The slice's measured defect class is putting 'at least' on a rolled figure, which can sit above the final one. The design guards it with fitness rule 1, but AtLeastSize takes a plain long, so every call site has to remember to pass the bound. Rule 1 matches only the exact spellings `Size`, `OnDisk`, `row.Bytes` and `row.OnDisk`, plus a Rolled* call inside the parentheses. These pass it quietly:
- AtLeastSize(this.OnDisk)
- AtLeastSize(onDisk) with a local copied from row.OnDisk
- AtLeastSize(r.Bytes) when the parameter is renamed
- AtLeastSize(OnDisk + 0)
The decided follow-up (Q-292) puts the listed figure on the same line as the bound, which is exactly where the wrong argument gets passed. The design also adds a second value type, TopLevelAtLeast (long Files), that duplicates ScanStore.AtLeastFigures (int Files), and labels that public contract 'expensive' to reverse. That type exists only because AtLeastFigures is nested in ScanStore, which TopLevelSnapshot.cs may not name.
findings.evidence: .taad/fitness.yaml:1398-1399 (rule 1 patterns); src/FsAnalyser.Core/Store/ScanStore.cs:272 (AtLeastFigures nested in ScanStore); design key_decisions 'The row field is a new Core value type, TopLevelAtLeast' (reversibility expensive); Q-292 follow-up
findings.fix:
Move the invariant into the seam:
- Move AtLeastFigures out of ScanStore into its own Store file as a readonly struct whose constructor is internal to Core. The name ScanStore is then not needed, so TopLevelSnapshot.cs may carry it.
- Make TopLevelRow.AtLeast an `AtLeastFigures?` and drop TopLevelAtLeast.
- Give TopLevelRowText AtLeastSizeText(AtLeastFigures) and AtLeastOnDiskText(AtLeastFigures) in place of AtLeastSize(long).
The App can then format only a bound the store produced, and rule 1 (with its harness churn) can be dropped.

findings.claim:
The design's validate command list (the 'cli' contract) leaves out four checks:
- eng/rules-harness/harness.py. Q-027, a human decision, requires it at validate of any slice that changes .taad/fitness.yaml, and this slice appends two rules (the worktree shows fitness.yaml modified).
- RuleCases C-001 and C-003, which lesson #486 says move with any fitness.yaml append.
- WindowCases T-003. Q-128, a human decision, requires it at validate for slices touching FolderTreeNode or MainWindow's tree. Q-279 explains it reads VOID on this display; it does not drop it.
- The other existing window cases over the completed tree and the layout that the XAML widening touches, such as T-001 and T-004. Criterion 6 says 'the existing window cases pass unchanged', not only the stopped ones.
The design names the harness cost in its rationale but never puts the command in a case or in the validate list (CC-004).
findings.evidence: design contract 'WindowCases.ps1 -Case T-013 | T-014; WindowMutants.ps1 ...' notes ('At validate: the full Core suite; WindowCases T-013, T-014, L-001, L-004, T-010, T-011 and T-012 ... and WindowMutants -Mutant All'); Q-027; Q-128; Q-279; lesson #486; criterion 6
findings.fix:
Add four things to the validate list:
- harness.py --engine-root (Q-027).
- RuleCases -Case C-001 and -Case C-003.
- WindowCases -Case T-003, recording its known taller-window VOID line and the five open timings.
- Each remaining existing window case that reads the tree or the main window's layout, each as its own command under the 120 s limit.

findings.claim: StoppedTopLevel is a new scan-end pass that reads the store and is designed to throw InvalidOperationException on a row/child mismatch. It runs at line 301 inside StartScan's continuation, before ShowOutcome and outside any containment. Q-071 (human) and Q-158 decided that in interactive mode each scan-end pass is wrapped: a throw hides that panel and says 'Could not show …', with no global Handled=true. Built as designed, an impossible-state throw, or any ArgumentOutOfRangeException from a store read, takes down the whole stopped ending, and the person loses the result. Falling back to the unmarked TopLevel would also be wrong, because unmarked rows claim to be final.
findings.evidence: src/FsAnalyser.App/MainWindow.xaml.cs:301; design contract 'ScanResult.StoppedTopLevel()' error_cases ('Throws InvalidOperationException ... fails loudly'); Q-071, Q-158

quote.text: ShowFinalTopLevel(failure is null && result?.Status != ScanStatus.Completed ? result?.TopLevel : null);

findings.fix: Wrap the StoppedTopLevel call as Q-071 wraps the other scan-end passes. On a throw, clear the list (ShowFinalTopLevel(null)) and show 'Couldn't show this view: <type>: <message>'. Never fall back to the unmarked snapshot. Report mode stays exit 70.

findings.claim: For criterion 6 the design argues that 'PendingRun is false once the watermark equals Count, so Unfinished is false everywhere'. But Unfinished checks NotListedAtOrBelow before PendingRun. On a Completed store, 'no at least anywhere' therefore also needs every folder's NotListed bit to have been cleared by SetChildren. That is exactly what the risk spike 'completed-whole-c-nothing-unfinished' was asking, and it did not finish: the scan was not run because it needs a person's OK. The design does not mention this. The two surfaces are also guarded differently. StoppedTopLevel returns the unmarked snapshot for Completed results, but the tree's Bound read has no status guard and runs on every completed tree. A single NotListed folder left in a real completed scan would put 'at least' on its whole chain up to the root, and no case would see it, because the planned criterion-6 check uses only the fixture tree.
findings.evidence: src/FsAnalyser.Core/Store/ScanStore.cs:208-209; risk spike completed-whole-c-nothing-unfinished ('scan not run (needs OK)'); design case 'show nothing as at least after a scan that ran to the end' (why); design contract for StoppedTopLevel (Completed guard) vs component 'Tree row at-least figures' (no guard)
findings.fix: Correct the stated reasoning and record that criterion 6 on real drives rests on the unrun spike. Then either give FolderTreeSession the stopped-ending condition (Cancelled, TopLevel final and not completed), so the tree reads the bound under exactly the guard StoppedTopLevel uses, or keep the asymmetry deliberately and say so.

findings.claim: The two new mutants remove the marks entirely: NoTreeAtLeast returns a null bound, and NoListAtLeast skips the marking read. Neither exercises the defect class the slice was built around, which is the word on a rolled figure, nor the spike's no-go, a revert to 80 DIP cells. T-013 has checks aimed at both: drawn equals storeAtLeast and differs from storeRolled on at least one row, and the cell-fit line. But no run shows those lines can turn red (CC-013).
findings.evidence: design component 'Mutants that remove the marks'; design case 'draw an at least figure in full'; risk spike at-least-prefix-drawn-unclipped
findings.fix:
Add two mutants and pin the exact FAIL lines T-013 must print for each:
- TreeAtLeastRolled, which formats the rolled Size and OnDisk with the word.
- NarrowAtLeastCells, which sets Width 102 back to 80 in MainWindow.xaml.

dimensions_checked.result: m3: the criterion-6 reasoning skips Unfinished's NotListedAtOrBelow arm, which is the unrun whole-C spike's question. Verified against code: Unfinished's arm order (ScanStore.cs:201-224), AtLeast's subtraction (239-269), AtLeastFigures nested with int Files (272), the tracker's row i = _first+i seeding (TopLevelTracker.cs:46-73), and that the Rows count is the root listing count. Cross-domain must-verify precondition (ancestor propagation): if traversal order changes (U-197 per-block SetChildren, parallel listing), Unfinished(parent) can read false over an unfinished child. The App does no walk, so the ancestor shows as final under a header that promises it, with no error. Fact (d) on a ragged tree cannot see a per-block registration in a folder over the 2,000-entry sweeps (lesson #510), and T-013 checks only T-010's fixture. This is SL-111/SL-112's standing condition, not new, so no separate finding.

M1: unmarked share percentages are not final, against the header's 'a figure with no mark is final'. Checked and fine:
- A NotScanned row is unfinished-false and keeps its title mark.
- A hardlink later name is never pending, and charges do not move between names (U-130).
- A pending top-level file reads 'at least 0 bytes'.
- Folder and unreadable counts in the marked FiguresOf arm are true lower bounds.
- Revised plus AtLeast on one row is coherent.
- RootUnreadable, Refused and Count-0 endings all return TopLevel unchanged.
- The timer is stopped (line 287) before line 301, so no tick can redraw the unmarked final snapshot.
- ShowStoppedList redraws from _shownTopLevel, so the marked snapshot survives switching between list and tree.

M3: the rolled-vs-bound invariant is held by discipline plus a regex with holes, when a typed parameter (the store's bound type, internal constructor) would make the mistake impossible to write. The tree/list predicate (Unfinished && !NotListed) is written twice, in FolderTreeNode (via HasFigures) and in WithAtLeast. T-013 C4 cross-checks it, so I left it as a note.

TopLevelAtLeast duplicates ScanStore.AtLeastFigures, folded into M3. Two narrow regex rules bring rules-harness and RuleCases churn (lesson #486) for a guard the types could give for nothing. T-014 rebuilds T-012's 100k fixture, and T-012's stopped half already opens the 100k folder with marks in place once the App draws them. That choice is a recorded taste disagreement, so I left it alone. In StoppedTopLevel the Count==0 guard is unreachable, because Count 0 implies TopLevel null and the earlier guard returns first. The 'root never listed' case therefore exercises the TopLevel-null guard (CC-005). The outcome is still right, so this is not a finding.

Checked:
- StoppedTopLevel returns a new object whenever a row is marked, which gets past ShowFinalTopLevel's reference-equal skip (MainWindow.xaml.cs:370).
- WithRows copies every init property TopLevelSnapshot has today (StoppedInSizeChecks is the only one).
- The row copy restates Revised and FailedKind, the only init properties on TopLevelRow, and Fact (a)'s reflection compare would catch a later property the copy forgets, but only if a fixture gives it a non-default value.
- TopLevelRow.AtLeast is init-only, and only Core can construct a TopLevelRow (internal constructor), so the App cannot fabricate a marked row.
No gap beyond M3 and m2.

m2: the fail-loud throw at the ending is outside Q-071/Q-158's per-pass containment. Tree-side reads sit in OneTime binding getters, where an exception becomes a trace line and an empty cell rather than a crash. That is acceptable, and T-013's per-row compare would expose it.

m1: the validate list omits checks that Q-027 (rules harness), Q-128 (T-003) and criterion 6 (all existing window cases) require. Checked as consistent with the decided questions: Q-290 (the listing and sizing headers keep their lead and not-read explanation, and only the two pinned constants move; the tree header is pinned only by StartsWith($StoppedTreeLead) at WindowCases.ps1:6636-6637, so appending is legal), Q-291, Q-292 (follow-up filed), Q-293 (no tree count column), Q-276 (NotRead line unchanged), Q-277 (list-first kept), Q-114/Q-115 (mutants in the roster) and Q-222 (separate cases).

Checked the design's code against the rules in .taad/fitness.yaml:
- 'Core does not publish a live ScanStore' (564-586): TopLevelSnapshot.cs is not on the allow-list; ScanResult.cs and TopLevelTracker.cs are.
- 'only the tracker sets Revised' (850-859).
- 'published snapshot types cannot be changed' (495-509): `public readonly record struct` and `{ get; init; }` pass all five patterns.
- 'the window never touches the scan store' (472-494): result?.StoppedTopLevel() matches none of its patterns.
- 'a tree row's figure text is never guarded by the store alone' (1368-1378): the design keeps HasFigures first.
- 'the unread word is written once' (1350-1365): the headers use NotReadYet.
The two appended SL-113 rules (1395-1417) are quiet on the tree today. The only App 'at least' text is a comment at FolderTreeRowText.cs:23 with no quote character on the line. Being 'settled' rules, they need no xUnit twin, consistent with the file's convention. M3 covers CC-007's variant holes. One more hole: rule 2 does not cover *.xaml, so a ToolTip literal 'at least' escapes it. The new hook reflection follows the existing TitleOf pattern.

M2: header checks read strings, not drawn characters. m4: no mutant shows that the drawn-equals-bound check or the cell-fit check can fail. Fine: T-013 C1-C4 read the store's own answers through the hook (lesson #310), not row properties, and the WALK fixtures respect WalkLimit (c-prefix's 5,000 children is read as a row, not opened). T-014's VOID rule covers the recalled NTFS-order claim. The Core Facts cover the field-preserving copy and the new-object contract that no window case can force.
none: a local read-only display change over the app's own in-memory store. No new file, process, network or privilege surface, and no elevation needed.
